title: Thin-Film & Flexible Electronics
question: How does printed-film thickness shape electrical differences between nominally identical stretchable interconnects?
whatIControl: Doctor-blade print thickness · trace geometry · process uniformity
whatIMeasure: Initial trace-to-trace electrical variability separately from resistance changes under repeated deformation.
whyItMatters: Process uniformity and electrical reliability require distinct measurements of initial nonuniformity and mechanical cycling.
scope: Research experience includes flexible interconnects, stretchable PCB technologies, and mechanically robust films in deformable electronic systems.
evidence: Participation in these programs extends device and materials research to mechanical deformation.
homeDescription: Printing variability, stretchable interconnects, and electrical reliability.

paragraphs.text: Research experience includes flexible interconnects, stretchable PCB technologies, and mechanically robust films in deformable electronic systems.
These programs extend my device research toward transport and reliability under mechanical deformation.

foundationText: First-author work examines how doctor-blade-printed film thickness contributes to electrical variability between liquid-metal-particle interconnect traces. Initial differences are evaluated separately from resistance changes under repeated deformation; related flexible-device programs extend this process–structure–property foundation.
